newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Handelsbanken prospectus seen in order.
newsitem.headline: Handelsbanken prospectus seen in order.

text.p: A prospectus from Swedish bank Handelsbanken for its 22.9 billion crown cash bid for mortgage lender Stadshypotek was quite normal and in order despite criticism in one newspaper, analysts said on Friday.
"As it is a cash bid, the prospectus does not have to be fuller," said Jonny Sylven, analyst at Swedbank.
"Some would have liked a more thorough presentation of Stadshypotek in the prospectus, but that is probably not in Handelsbanken's interest."
Swedish daily newspaper Dagens Nyheter said on Thursday the prospectus with about 20 pages may not be sufficiently comprehensive to convince shareholders to accept the bid.

The paper's stockmarket commentator compared the prospectus with insurer Skandia AB's now withdrawn prospectus for a merger with Stadshypotek, finding that Skandia's prospectus contained 10 times more pages.
But neither Handelsbanken nor analysts found the two comparable as a merger proposal means shareholders keep their shares and so they remain interested in the company.
With a cash bid, shareholders solely focus on the price as they will not have anything to do with the future company.
The Swedish shareholders' association, which reiterated its recommendation that Stadshypotek owners accept the cash bid, did not find the size of the prospectus alarming.
"But we would like a rule that says that all bidders will have to present themselves to shareholders in the prospectus," said Lars Milberg.
"In this case that may seem unnecessary as most people in Sweden know what Handelsbanken is, but in principle we would like such a rule."
Handelsbanken's head of corporate finance, Kjell Ormegard, said the managements of Stadshypotek and Skandia had planned a merger together while Handelsbanken merely placed a bid.
"Before we placed the bid, we had not talked to Stadshypotek's management, so we do not know how we will reorganise the company," Ormegard said.
"We were merely invited by the finance ministry to place a bid (on the government's 34 percent Stadshypotek stake)."
Ormegard said the bank will discuss plans for reorganisation with Stadshypotek's management when the bank has control of the mortgage lender and then have more details.
